'''Silvia''' — online as '''@ailaughatmyownjokes''' — is a sketch-comedy creator from '''South Tyrol''', the German-speaking Alpine region of northern Italy, which is why her work slides between Italian and German. She built an enormous following on TikTok and YouTube, and what sets her apart is that she is a '''one-person universe''': she writes and performs a whole cast of '''original characters''' entirely herself. She appears in [[Media and Personalities]] as a '''YouTuber entry''', covered for what she actually makes.

== The Silviaverse ==

Her signature is the '''"Silviaverse"''' — a sprawling, interconnected cast of her own invented characters, all played by Silvia, built up across recurring series rather than borrowed from existing franchises. She does the voices, the costumes, the bits, and the running continuity; the humor is offbeat, meme-forward, and tips into '''creepypasta / internet-horror-adjacent''' territory — strange, slightly unsettling, and very online rather than straight stand-up.

The flagship is '''Villain Silvia''', the star of the '''"If I were a villain"''' series: a gleeful super-villainess with an eye-patch who swears constantly and delights in committing crimes and doing evil — forever being corrected and reined in by her long-suffering assistant '''Marcus'''. Around her Silvia keeps a roster of other recurring originals that populate the same universe, so returning viewers follow characters and callbacks, not one-off gags.

== Her other formats ==

Alongside the Silviaverse she does '''fandom roleplay skits''' — short in-character scenes set inside popular worlds (Harry Potter, The Walking Dead, Scream, The Hunger Games and others) — and she frequently collaborates with her roommate '''@redheadbegins''', who makes similar videos, including joint series such as ''OnlyCakes''. Her reach runs to several million followers, and her bits circulate widely through reaction and compilation uploads.

== Why she fits the Library ==

A single creator building and inhabiting an entire fictional universe — doing every character herself, with continuity and lore — is exactly the kind of one-mind-many-voices worldbuilding the Library finds interesting: it rhymes with the [[Egregore]] idea of a self that holds many personae, and with the internet-native, slightly-haunted storytelling the section tracks elsewhere ([[Sarah Davis Baker]]). We note her as a standout example of the form.
